coldOpen: That tiny jeans pocket was not designed for loose change.
centralQuestion: Why do jeans have a tiny pocket above the larger front pocket?

evidence.claim: The small front-right pocket on classic Levi's jeans is called a watch pocket.
evidence.source: Levi Strauss & Co. Archives — Pockets Full of History

evidence.claim: The watch pocket was intended to hold a pocket watch, a common possession in the late nineteenth century.
evidence.source: Levi Strauss & Co. Archives — Pockets Full of History

evidence.claim: The small watch pocket was part of the original riveted waist overalls introduced in 1873.
evidence.source: Levi Strauss & Co. historian — The Story Behind the Official Fifth Pocket

evidence.claim: Levi Strauss and Jacob Davis received a United States patent for improving the fastening of pocket openings in 1873.
evidence.source: Levi Strauss & Co. Archives — Pockets Full of History

evidence.claim: Copper rivets strengthened pocket openings and helped keep them from ripping.
evidence.source: Levi Strauss & Co. Archives — Pockets Full of History

evidence.claim: The original trousers were known as waist overalls.
evidence.source: Levi Strauss & Co. historian — The Story Behind the Official Fifth Pocket

evidence.claim: The original waist overalls had four pockets in total.
evidence.source: Levi Strauss & Co. historian — The Story Behind the Official Fifth Pocket

evidence.claim: Those four pockets were two large front pockets, the watch pocket, and one back pocket.
evidence.source: Levi Strauss & Co. historian — The Story Behind the Official Fifth Pocket

evidence.claim: Levi Strauss and Company describes the watch pocket as protection for a pocket watch.
evidence.source: Levi Strauss & Co. Archives — Those Oft-Forgotten Pant Parts

evidence.claim: The tiny front pocket is sometimes called the fifth pocket, but it was part of the original four-pocket arrangement.
evidence.source: Levi Strauss & Co. historian — The Story Behind the Official Fifth Pocket

evidence.claim: A second back pocket was added in 1901.
evidence.source: Levi Strauss & Co. historian — The Story Behind the Official Fifth Pocket

evidence.claim: The back pocket added in 1901 is the actual fifth pocket in the documented design sequence.
evidence.source: Levi Strauss & Co. historian — The Story Behind the Official Fifth Pocket

evidence.claim: During the Second World War, rivets were removed from the watch pocket to save metal.
evidence.source: Levi Strauss & Co. Archives — Pockets Full of History

evidence.claim: The watch-pocket rivets were restored after the wartime change.
evidence.source: Levi Strauss & Co. Archives — Pockets Full of History

evidence.claim: The original waist overalls also used a button fly, copper rivets, blue denim, and arcuate stitching.
evidence.source: Levi Strauss & Co. historian — The Story Behind the Official Fifth Pocket

evidence.claim: The watch pocket remains part of the familiar five-pocket jean design.
evidence.source: Levi Strauss & Co. historian — The Story Behind the Official Fifth Pocket
